sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Pennsauken different?
sections.html:
Pennsauken requires a housing resale inspection and a fire certificate on every one- and two-family house before settlement. The inspections happen on the township's schedule, so owners who plan around them close with fewer surprises.

The township lies in Camden County directly across the Delaware River from Philadelphia, joined to the city by the Betsy Ross Bridge, which opened April 30, 1976. It covers 10.48 square miles of land plus 1.65 of water, was set off from Stockton Township and incorporated on February 18, 1892, and had an estimated 37,742 residents in mid-2025. Petty's Island, a 392-acre island in the river, belongs to Pennsauken, and the Camden Drive-In, the first drive-in theater in America, opened here in 1933.

Industry shapes the local map. A large industrial park holds a beverage bottling plant and a snack food manufacturer, and the old Pennsauken Mart site became a luxury apartment complex completed in 2018 after the market closed in January 2006.

sections.h2: What does the Pennsauken housing resale inspection involve?
sections.html:
Township ordinance calls for an interior and exterior inspection plus a Certificate of Occupancy before settlement. The Building Department's packet lists a combined $175 fee, made up of $100 for the housing resale certificate and $75 for the fire certificate.

Sellers send both forms and payment to the Building Department, then wait about two to three days after the visit for a written report. The housing office takes scheduling calls at 856-665-1000, extension 145, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Certificates cover one change of ownership or six months, whichever ends first. The application also asks whether the buyer plans to flip the house, rent it or live in it, and whether the property is vacant, rented or owner-occupied.

If the report lists repairs, the buyer may sign a notarized affidavit for a temporary certificate, accepting the report and responsibility for the final certificate. When the report forbids occupancy before a final certificate, the temporary version covers work only. Open construction permits must be inspected and closed first, and the packet warns that missed permits can push back a settlement date.

sections.h2: Which fire safety items does Pennsauken check?
sections.html:
The fire certificate looks at alarms and extinguishers, with smoke alarm rules that depend on the year the house was built.

  • Before 1975: sealed 10-year battery alarms only.
  • 1975 to 1977: a hardwired detector on the top level and sealed battery alarms elsewhere.
  • 1977 to 1983: interconnected hardwired alarms on the top level and in the basement, battery alarms on other levels.
  • 1983 to 1991: interconnected hardwired alarms on every level.
  • 1991 on: interconnected hardwired alarms with battery backup on every level and in each bedroom.

A carbon monoxide alarm must sit within ten feet of every sleeping area, and combination units are accepted. At least one extinguisher rated 2A:10-BC, no heavier than ten pounds, must hang within ten feet of the kitchen with its top three to five feet above the floor, and carry a service tag from the last 365 days or a dated receipt if new.

sections.h2: What does the resale checklist catch in a Pennsauken house?
sections.html:
The inspector's checklist follows the property maintenance code and runs well beyond alarms.

  • Exterior: grading and drainage, sidewalks and driveways, accessory structures, roofs and drainage, foundation walls, and decks, porches and stairs.
  • Interior: structural members, walls and floors, stair surfaces, handrails and guards, and any sign of infestation.
  • Systems: roof, plumbing, mechanical and electrical certifications, hazard checks, at least two outlets per room except bathrooms, and GFCI protection near sinks and outdoors.
  • Records: open permits and occupancy limits, such as minimum room widths and bedroom access.

Rental registration and a lead paint visual assessment application sit on the same housing forms page, so a house that has been a rental may need extra paperwork.

sections.h2: Who buys in Pennsauken, and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey puts the typical value of an owner-occupied Pennsauken home at $232,900, with 73.9 percent of homes occupied by their owners. Median gross rent is $1,209, median household income is $87,680, and the mean commute is 25.5 minutes.

The population is 39.5 percent Hispanic or Latino, 18.3 percent foreign-born, and 40.8 percent of residents age five and over speak another language at home. About 13.9 percent live below the poverty line. Households average 2.87 people across 12,900 homes.

Pennsauken Public Schools enrolled 4,828 students in ten schools in 2022 to 2023. Pennsauken Technical High School serves students countywide, while Eustace Preparatory School and St. Cecilia School are private schools inside the township.

sections.h2: How does getting around Pennsauken affect a sale?
sections.html:
Buyers who commute notice three things quickly: highways, trains and the bridge. U.S. 130 is the largest road, meeting Route 73 near the Cinnaminson line, while Route 90 leads to the Betsy Ross Bridge. Route 38, Route 70 and U.S. 30 meet at the Airport Circle junction, a site once called the first highway traffic circle in the country.

NJ Transit's River Line stops at Pennsauken Route 73 and 36th Street, and the Pennsauken Transit Center on River Road, opened October 2013 at a $40 million cost, connects the River Line with the Atlantic City Line. Bus routes 317, 404, 406 and 409 run daily to Philadelphia.

The climate is humid subtropical. Recorded extremes run from 108 degrees Fahrenheit on July 16, 1995 to minus 4 degrees in January 1994, and 13.59 percent of the township's area is water, so expect buyers to ask about drainage and basement history.

sections.h2: How do Pennsauken taxes and recording work?
sections.html:
The township mails one bill each summer. It combines a final bill for the current year and a preliminary bill for the next, with four stubs due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. An added or omitted assessment bill follows in October. Late payments after the grace period, usually the 10th, accrue interest from the due date at 8 percent on the first $1,500 and 18 percent above it, and a December 31 delinquency over $10,000 adds a 6 percent penalty.

Office hours at 2400 Merchantville Avenue run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. weekdays, with a drop box outside. Online payments carry a processing fee set by the provider, not the township. Owners who change mailing address should tell the assessor.

Deeds are recorded at the Camden County Clerk's office, Room 102, 520 Market Street in Camden, phone 856-225-5300. Electronic recording and online record searching are both available. Sellers who live in New Jersey use the residency certification form with the deed, and a co-signer who gets no proceeds can use the no-net-proceeds box, entering zero consideration.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale a practical choice in Pennsauken?
sections.html:
Cash tends to suit a house that cannot pass the resale report without major work, a vacant property that has sat, or an inheritance the heirs want settled. The buyer can sign the affidavit for a temporary certificate and take over repairs, which lets the closing proceed.

Ask every buyer who pays the $175, who books the inspection, and how long the offer stands if the report is long. Judge offers by your net after repairs and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Does Pennsauken require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. All one- and two-family dwellings need a housing resale inspection and a Certificate of Occupancy before settlement, and the Building Department lists a $175 combined fee with the fire certificate.

faqs.q: Can the buyer take responsibility for repairs in Pennsauken?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer who accepts the report can sign a notarized affidavit for a temporary Certificate of Occupancy and take on the listed items. If the report bars occupancy, the temporary certificate covers work only.

faqs.q: How long is a Pennsauken resale certificate good for?
faqs.a: It covers one change of ownership or six months, whichever comes first. Schedule the inspection close enough to settlement that the certificate does not expire first.

faqs.q: When are Pennsauken property taxes due?
faqs.a: The stubs are due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. A grace period, usually to the 10th, applies before interest runs back to the due date.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Pennsauken sale?
faqs.a: At the Camden County Clerk, Room 102 at 520 Market Street in Camden. Electronic recording is also accepted, and the office can be reached at 856-225-5300.
